tree.player: Seriously, you came up here by helicopter? This mountain used to be a glacier, and now look at it.
tree.persona: I came here by helicopter because it's the most efficient way to get here. The glacier's gone, but that doesn't mean the climate isn't changing. I just don't think we need to panic about it. What do you think caused the glacier to disappear?

children.player: Fair enough, there was no road up here anyway, and you're right that panicking doesn't help. But I think it's mostly the warming we've caused, don't you?
children.persona: I don’t disagree with that, but I still think the problems are overblown. What do you think the main cause was—nature or humans?

children.player: Both play a role, sure. But glaciers used to take thousands of years to change, and this one went in a few decades. That's mostly us.
children.persona: I see your point, but glaciers have always changed slowly. What’s the real driver here—nature or human activity?

children.player: You're asking me the same thing again. I said it: human activity. That's exactly why it changed so fast this time.
children.persona: I agree it’s human activity that’s speeding things up. But how do you know it’s not just natural cycles acting faster this time?

children.persona: I agree it’s the extra CO2 that’s pushing things faster. But how do you know it’s not just the climate changing naturally, like it has before?

children.player: I already told you, humans. And I don't think it's overblown when you're looking at bare rock where there was ice twenty years ago.
children.persona: I agree it's humans, but I still think the impact is exaggerated. What do you think the real problem is—climate change or something else?

children.player: Climate change is the real problem. Losing a glacier means less water for the valleys below in summer, that's not exaggerated.
children.persona: I see the logic in what you're saying, but I still think the bigger picture is more complicated. What do you think the main threat is—glaciers disappearing or something else?

children.player: It's complicated, I get that. But the glacier is one of the clearest signs we have, so I'd start there instead of looking for something else.
children.persona: I agree the glacier is a clear sign, but I still think the bigger picture is more complicated. What do you think the real cause is—human activity or something else?

children.player: I understand it's efficient, but scientists agree the glacier melted because of human-caused warming. Doesn't flying in here feel a bit contradictory to you?
children.persona: I know scientists say it's human-caused, but I’ve seen glaciers melt before. It’s part of the cycle, I guess. What’s your take on why this one disappeared?

children.player: Glaciers do go through cycles, but those take thousands of years. This one vanished in one lifetime, natural cycles can't explain that speed.
children.persona: I’ve seen glaciers shrink before, but I don’t think it’s all human-caused. What’s your take on how fast this one melted?

children.player: Way faster than any natural cycle. Old photos of this valley show ice everywhere, and it's gone in a few decades.
children.persona: I’ve been here before, and the ice was there. But I don’t think that proves anything. What do you make of the photos?

children.player: They show the ice was there for centuries and melted in one generation. If you saw it yourself, doesn't that make you wonder a little?
children.persona: I’ve been here before, and the ice was there. But I don’t think that proves anything. What do you make of the photos?

children.player: Part of the cycle? That's just an excuse so you don't have to change anything! You keep dodging my question about the helicopter.
children.persona: I don’t deny the climate is changing, but I’ve seen glaciers come and go. You’re right, it’s not an excuse—but I still don’t think it justifies flying here. What’s your view on how much we can rely on technology to fix things?

children.player: Thanks for admitting that. Technology can help, but it won't be enough if we keep flying everywhere for convenience.
children.persona: I’m not denying technology can help, but I’ve seen it fail before. Why do you think flying is any better than driving?

children.player: I didn't say driving was better. I'm saying the best trip here is the one done by train and on foot, it's possible.
children.persona: I’ve seen people do it the hard way, but I don’t think the climate’s going to stop us from getting where we need to. What’s the point of a trip if you can’t get there?

children.player: So you know it's not justified and you did it anyway? And now you want technology to clean up after you?
children.persona: I know it's not justified, but I have to get here for work. Technology will handle the cleanup, I’m sure of it. What do you think will be the first thing they fix?

children.player: You're sure of it? That's not a plan, that's wishful thinking! Nobody is going to fix this for you.
children.persona: I came here for work, not to make excuses. Technology will handle the mess, I’m sure of it. What do you think will be the first thing they fix?

children.player: What caused it? People like you burning fuel for convenience! You're standing on the proof and you still say there's no reason to worry?
children.persona: I didn’t cause it, and I don’t think we should blame everyone for everything. But I do think we need to find solutions that work, not just point fingers. What’s your take on how we should approach this?

children.player: Okay, you're right, shouting at each other won't fix it. I'd start with cutting the trips we don't really need, like flights for short distances.
children.persona: I didn’t come here to argue, just to see what’s left of the glacier. But I do think we’re overreacting. What’s your real concern?

children.player: My concern is that we are already losing places like this one. I don't think it's overreacting when the ice is literally gone.
children.persona: I didn’t come here to argue, just to see what’s left of the glacier. But I do think we’re overreacting. What’s your real concern?

children.persona: I came here to see what’s left, not to fight. You’re right, the ice is gone. But what’s the real problem?

children.persona: I don’t pretend to have all the answers, but I do think we should focus on what works, not just what’s easy. What do you think the real problem is here?
